html: <sherpa-markdown-editor name="message" data-label="Message" data-description="What the reader gets: Markdown, with values" placeholder="Write the message"

value="## Patch plan
Hi {{value:recipient.first_name}},
**{{value:runs.planned}} Runs** are planned for {{value:customer.name}}:
- Servers: an *MSP admin* approves first
- Workstations: tonight">
use: For a long text a reader formats — a message, a note, a runbook's steps — written in Markdown and shown as it reads as they type, with a switch to the Markdown itself. Its `value` is the Markdown; `{{value:node.name}}` values read as purple chips (`.valueLabels` gives their words), and `insertValue(key)` puts one at the caret. For one line of plain text, use `sherpa-input-text`; for a chat prompt, `sherpa-prompt-composer`.
